My friend recently gave me three bags of what I'm almost 100% sure are jalapeño peppers, and I really want to make something out of them. I've already made all of the salsa I can handle, but I'm still left with 2 bags of peppers. These are what the peppers look like. Any suggestions are much appreciated!
What can I make with a lot of jalapeños?

We make "hot pepper pepper." Basically cut up the peppers and put on a parchment lined baking sheet and place them in the oven on the lowest heat until they are dry. It will take quite a few hours. Then grind them up in a coffee grinder and mix in a small amount of garlic powder. We use this powder to add heat to dishes without really altering the flavor too much.
Dry some, use soil to flavour oil, use the rest in cooking.

If they're serranos, per @FoodGeekFish, I would suggest making verde sauce (usually for enchiladas, but it's yummy over lots of things).

Just toss tomatillos, onion, garlic, cumin, cilantro, lime juice, salt & pepper, and the serranos in a blender or food processor. Blammo. Delicious.
You could try jalapeno poppers (stuffed with cream cheese and breaded). They are pretty easy and super yummy. And it sounds random, but they are really yummy when dipped in strawberry jam.

TL/DR Apple fanboys who can't afford an iPhone. (No mention of other MP3 players, just that the buyers don't have smartphones of their own. A full android phone costs less than an iPod, so it's literally just Fanboys without iPhones.)

I don't have an iPad, but I have a dedicated mp3 player - and I have a smart phone.

I prefer the mp3 player for my commute because it has actual buttons. I can change tracks and slide volume without looking at the thing. With my smartphone, I have to take it out and look at it. With regular use, my smartphone will run 3 days without a charge. If I use it as an mp3 player, I have to charge it sooner. The mp3 player is charged about every 2 weeks.

I have bought multiple Shuffles for myself...

I use them when doing yard work. There's nothing like spending a couple of minutes loading your Playlist onto the thing before going out for a Saturday of cutting grass and pulling weeds. There's no screen to break, it uses minimal power since it doesn't have to light an LED panel, and I don't get WiFi on the outskirts of my yard, so I'm not interested in that aspect.

For $50, it works perfectly!
